newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down on late greenback demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down on late greenback demand.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower on Wednesday on strong, late U.S. dollar demand from a local bank known to often conduct foreign exchange transactions on behalf of Taiwan's military, dealer said.
The local unit ended at an intra-day low of T$27.540 against Tuesday's T$27.521 close.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$338 million.
"In the last half hour, strong U.S. dollar demand from one local bank emerged, and the bank always represents the military to buy U.S. dollars," said one dealer.
The military frequently buys U.S. dollars for payments on overseas purchases of military equipment.
Dealers also said the Taiwan dollar's fall reflected the strength of the U.S. dollar overseas.
But dealers saw limited room for the local dollar to fall.
Persistent inflows of foreign equity funds and tightening liquidity in the domestic money market should offset the Taiwan dollar depreciation, they said.
Investors tend to sell U.S. dollars in exchange for Taiwan dollars when facing tightening liquidity, dealers said. For Thursday, a T$27.52-55 range was seen.-James Peng (5080815)
